title: The Commuting Local Hamiltonian Problem: Relativized Evidence Against BQP-Hardness
abstract: The commuting local-Hamiltonian (CLH) problem is a restriction of the local-Hamiltonian problem, in which the terms of the Hamiltonian are required to pairwise commute. A long line of work has shown that the problem lies in $\mathsf{NP}$ for certain families of commuting local Hamiltonians. Nevertheless, there has been no formal evidence against the possibility that the general CLH problem is $\mathsf{QMA}$-complete.   CLH is complete for the complexity class $\mathsf{QIMA}$, defined through quantum verifiers whose local gates commute. Therefore, CLH is $\mathsf{QMA}$-complete if and only if $\mathsf{QIMA}=\mathsf{QMA}$. In this work, we introduce a classical-oracle analogue $\mathsf{QIMA}^{\mathcal{O}}$ and construct a classical oracle $\mathcal{O}$ such that $\mathsf{BQP}^{\mathcal{O}}\not\subseteq\mathsf{QIMA}^{\mathcal{O}}$.   Since $\mathsf{BQP}^{\mathcal{O}}\subseteq\mathsf{QMA}^{\mathcal{O}}$ for any classical oracle $\mathcal{O}$, this implies $\mathsf{QIMA}^{\mathcal{O}}\neq\mathsf{QMA}^{\mathcal{O}}$ for our constructed oracle. Thus, our result provides relativized evidence against the possibility that the general commuting local-Hamiltonian problem is $\mathsf{BQP}$-hard, and hence also against the possibility that it is $\mathsf{QMA}$-complete.
summary: This paper analyzes the computational complexity of the Commuting Local Hamiltonian (CLH) problem, showing it is complete for the class QIMA. By constructing a specific classical oracle, the authors prove a separation between $	ext{BQP}^{\mathcal{O}}$ and $	ext{QIMA}^{\mathcal{O}}$, providing strong evidence that the general CLH problem is not as hard as $	ext{QMA}$-complete.
main_problem: The paper investigates the computational complexity of the Commuting Local Hamiltonian (CLH) problem, a restriction of the local-Hamiltonian problem where Hamiltonian terms must pairwise commute.
main_result:
The authors provide relativized evidence against the possibility that the general CLH problem is BQP-hard or QMA-complete by constructing an oracle separation ($	ext{BQP}^{\mathcal{O}}
ot\subseteq	ext{QIMA}^{\mathcal{O}}$).
method: The proof involves constructing a classical oracle $\mathcal{O}$ and utilizing the Forrelation problem to demonstrate that the complexity class $	ext{QIMA}^{\mathcal{O}}$ is strictly different from $	ext{QMA}^{\mathcal{O}}$.
model_or_system: The analysis is framed within quantum complexity theory, comparing the CLH problem (complete for $	ext{QIMA}$) against $	ext{QMA}$ and $	ext{BQP}$ using oracle constructions.
key_observables: The minimum eigenvalue ($\lambda_{\min}$) of the constructed commuting local Hamiltonian, which must be distinguished between $\le \alpha$ (YES) and $\ge  eta$ (NO).

main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the formal definition of $	ext{QIMA}$ and its oracle analogue $	ext{QIMA}^{\mathcal{O}}$, which relies on commuting local gates.
paper_structure:
The paper first establishes the $	ext{QIMA}$-completeness of the CLH problem, then introduces the oracle model $	ext{QIMA}^{\mathcal{O}}$, and finally uses the Forrelation problem and diagonalization techniques to prove the separation $	ext{BQP}^{\mathcal{O}}
ot\subseteq	ext{QIMA}^{\mathcal{O}}$.
why_interesting: The work directly addresses the computational hardness of quantum many-body problems (like finding ground states), which is central to quantum simulation and quantum computation theory.
